## What to do

Adapt the upstream SDK doc (tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/docs/sdk.md, 1149 lines) for our Elixir system.

## Upstream source

- tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/docs/sdk.md
- tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/examples/sdk/ (all example files)
- tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/ (core types)

## Output

Create docs/sdk.md

## How to adapt

This is a very long doc (1149 lines). Structure it in these sections:

### 1. Overview
Document our Elixir SDK equivalent. Instead of npm, users install via our umbrella project. Instead of `createAgentSession()`, document our `OctoPi.Coder.SessionManager` API.

### 2. Quick Start
Convert the TypeScript quick start to Elixir:
```elixir
# In an Elixir app:
alias OctoPi.Coder.SessionManager
alias OctoPi.Coder.SettingsManager

settings = SettingsManager.create()
sessions = SessionManager.continue_recent(path, settings)
# or: SessionManager.in_memory()
# or: SessionManager.open("/path/to/session.jsonl")
```

### 3. Core Concepts

**SessionManager**: Document our `OctoPi.Coder.SessionManager` module:
- `create(cwd)` — new persistent session
- `in_memory()` — no persistence
- `continue_recent(cwd, settings)` — continue most recent
- `open(path)` — open specific file
- Static: `list(cwd)`, `list_all(cwd)`

**AgentSession**: Document our `OctoPi.Agent.Session` module:
- `prompt(pid, text, opts)` — send prompt
- `steer(pid, text)` — queue steering
- `follow_up(pid, text)` — queue follow-up
- `abort(pid)` — abort current operation
- `subscribe(pid, handler)` — subscribe to events
- `set_model(pid, model)` — switch model
- `set_thinking_level(pid, level)` — set thinking level
- `cycle_model(pid)` — cycle to next model
- `wait_for_idle(pid)` — wait for agent to finish

**ResourceLoader**: Document our equivalent for discovering extensions, skills, prompts, themes, and context files.

### 4. Options Reference

**Directories**: Document our config directory structure:
- `~/.octo_pi/` for global config
- `.pi/` for project config

**Model**: Document how to select models:
- `OctoPi.AI.ModelRegistry` for model discovery
- `OctoPi.AI.get_model(provider, id)` for specific models
- `OctoPi.AI.ModelRegistry.get_available(registry)` for available models

**API Keys and OAuth**: Document our AuthStorage:
- `OctoPi.AI.AuthStorage` for credential management
- `set_runtime_api_key/3` for runtime overrides

**System Prompt**: Document our system prompt override mechanism.

**Tools**: Document our tool system:
- `OctoPi.Coder.Tool` behaviour
- Built-in tools: read, write, edit, ls, bash, grep, find
- `define_tool/1` for custom tools

**Extensions**: Document our extension loading via ResourceLoader.

**Skills**: Document our skill loading.

**Prompt Templates**: Document our prompt template system.

**Session Management**: Document all SessionManager tree API methods:
- `get_entries/1`, `get_tree/1`, `get_path/1`, `get_leaf_entry/1`
- `get_entry/2`, `get_children/2`
- `get_label/2`, `append_label_change/3`
- `branch/2`, `branch_with_summary/3`, `create_branched_session/2`
- `new_session/1`, `switch_session/2`, `fork/3`

**Settings Management**: Document our SettingsManager:
- `SettingsManager.create(cwd, agent_dir)` — load from files
- `SettingsManager.in_memory(settings)` — no file I/O
- `flush/1` for durability boundary
- `drain_errors/1` for error handling

### 5. Run Modes
Document our three run modes:
- Interactive mode (TUI)
- Print mode (`mix pi --print`)
- RPC mode (`mix pi --mode rpc`)

## What to preserve verbatim

- The SDK architecture concepts (session, agent, resource loader)
- The event subscription pattern
- The session tree API concepts
- The settings management semantics

## Key upstream references to include

- [createAgentSession](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts)
- [SessionManager](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts)
- [examples/sdk/](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/tree/main/packages/coding-agent/examples/sdk/)

## Testing the doc

After writing, verify:
1. All module names match our actual modules
2. All function signatures are accurate
3. The session tree API matches our implementation
4. The settings management semantics match ours
